experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, white sand, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boats depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and offer snorkeling opportunities in the crystal-clear Ionian Sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a guided food tour. Sample local cheeses like graviera and feta, cured meats, fresh olives, and honey. Visit nearby tavernas to taste traditional mezedes, spanakopita, and loukoumades (Greek honey donuts). A deeply authentic culinary immersion into everyday Greek food culture.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow lagoon-like waters. Wade across the sandbar to the small islet, snorkel among sea life, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful coastal settings. Accessible by local bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Santorini
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class where a local chef teaches you to prepare classic Greek dishes such as moussaka, tzatziki, fresh tomato fritters, and fava dip using locally sourced Santorinian ingredients. The class includes a sit-down meal with local wine, giving you skills and recipes to take home alongside unforgettable flavors.

experiences.name: Balos Lagoon Beach Boat Excursion
experiences.description: Sail to the magical Balos Lagoon on the northwestern tip of Crete, a UNESCO-protected area with exotic turquoise and pink-hued shallow waters. The boat trip includes a stop at Gramvousa Island with its Venetian castle ruins. Swim, snorkel, and soak in one of the most spectacular beach landscapes in all of the Mediterranean.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X96 express bus (€6) or metro to Piraeus port. Board an afternoon/evening ferry to Zakynthos (journey ~7 hours). Grab snacks and water at the port kiosk before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the ferry for the overnight crossing. Enjoy the sunset from the deck as you sail through the Ionian Sea. Grab a budget meal from the ferry cafeteria (gyros or spanakopita, ~€5–7).

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – in transit
meals.lunch: Grab a quick souvlaki wrap or tiropita from a kiosk near Athens airport or Piraeus port (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Ferry cafeteria – spanakopita, gyros wrap, or a simple Greek salad (~€5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry ticket in advance on anek.gr or ferries.gr to secure the best budget price. The X96 bus from Athens Airport to Piraeus runs every 20 minutes and is the cheapest transfer option (€6). Arrive at Piraeus port at least 45 minutes before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Arrive at Zakynthos Town port early morning. Take a local bus or shared taxi to Navagio Beach area (Volimes/Anafonitria village, ~€5–8 by bus). Check into your boutique stay near Navagio Beach. Freshen up and enjoy a simple Greek breakfast of yogurt with honey and fresh fruit at a local kafeneio in Anafonitria village (~€3–5).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Navagio Beach viewpoint (Shipwreck Lookout) – a short walk or drive from the village. Marvel at the iconic panoramic view of the famous Shipwreck Beach from the cliffs above. The view is completely free and absolutely stunning. Walk along the clifftop trail and take photos in the golden afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Anafonitria village on foot. Visit the small 15th-century Anafonitria Monastery (free entry). Stroll the quiet village streets and relax at a local taverna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local kafeneio in Anafonitria – Greek yogurt with honey, fresh bread, and Greek coffee (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a mini-market (olives, bread, local cheese, ~€4) and enjoy at the clifftop viewpoint
meals.dinner: Taverna in Anafonitria village – moussaka or stuffed tomatoes with house wine (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach itself is only accessible by boat – plan a boat trip for a later day. The clifftop viewpoint is free and open all day. Rest well tonight after the overnight ferry journey.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and take a boat trip to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach – the most iconic beach in Greece. Book a shared boat excursion from Porto Vromi port (~15 min drive, shared trip ~€15–20 per person). Arrive at the beach early to beat the crowds. Swim in the brilliant turquoise water and explore the famous rusted shipwreck on the white pebble beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion to the nearby Blue Caves (Kianoun Spileon) on the northern coast. Snorkel or swim in the electric-blue water inside the sea caves – an unforgettable experience. Return to Porto Vromi by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation and shower. Walk to a local taverna in Volimes village for a traditional dinner. Volimes is also known for its local honey and textiles – browse the small shops before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation or a quick Greek coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a local bakery (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to eat on Navagio Beach – local bread, feta, olives, and tomatoes from the mini-market (~€5)
meals.dinner: Taverna in Volimes – grilled fresh fish of the day with Greek salad and local bread (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Book the shared boat trip the evening before from Porto Vromi harbour or through your accommodation. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water as there is no shade on Navagio Beach. Arrive at Porto Vromi by 9:00 AM for the first boat to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus south to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) – the island's charming capital (~1 hour, ~€4). Explore the Venetian-influenced town on foot. Visit Solomos Square, the main piazza named after Greece's national poet Dionysios Solomos. Walk through the arcaded streets and admire the post-earthquake reconstruction architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos on Solomos Square (entry ~€4) – houses rescued icons and artifacts from churches destroyed in the 1953 earthquake. Then walk up to Zakynthos Castle (Bochali Hill) for panoramic views over the town and Ionian Sea (entry ~€3). The walk up through the pine-scented hill is beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the waterfront promenade (Strata Marina) as the evening cools. Browse the local shops and find a budget taverna in the backstreets of Zakynthos Town for dinner away from the tourist-priced waterfront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Bakery in Zakynthos Town – fresh tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee (~€3)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki pita wrap from a local grill shop in Zakynthos Town (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in the backstreets – pastitsada (local pasta dish) or sofrito (veal in white wine sauce) with house wine (~€11–14)

day_by_day.notes: Sofrito is a Zakynthian specialty – don't miss it! The bus from Anafonitria/Volimes to Zakynthos Town runs a few times daily; check the KTEL Zakynthos schedule in advance. Return bus to the north departs from the KTEL station in Zakynthos Town.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed morning at a quieter beach near your accommodation. Xigia Beach (north coast) is famous for its natural sulphur springs that bubble up from the seabed – swimming here feels like a natural spa. Access is free and the beach is less crowded than Navagio. Bring your own snorkelling gear if possible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi ride to Makris Gialos or Schiza Beach – two small, uncrowded pebble coves near the northern tip of the island. Swim, sunbathe, and relax. Bring a picnic lunch and enjoy the afternoon in peaceful surroundings with crystal-clear Ionian water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Anafonitria and enjoy a slow evening in the village. Find a local kafeneio (traditional Greek coffee house) and play backgammon or cards with locals over an ouzo or freddo espresso.

meals.breakfast: Prepare a simple breakfast at your accommodation – local honey, bread, and fruit from the village mini-market (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the beach – local cheese, olives, bread, fresh tomatoes, and a cold Mythos beer (~€6–7)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at accommodation using local market ingredients, or grab a gyros from a local takeaway in Volimes (~€3–4)

day_by_day.notes: Xigia's sulphur springs are a unique natural experience – the water is warm and slightly fizzy. The smell of sulphur is noticeable but mild. This is a great low-cost rest day after several busy days of travel and sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry from Zakynthos Town to Killini on the Peloponnese mainland (~1 hour, ~€8–10). From Killini, take a bus to Patras (~1.5 hours, ~€5). Explore Patras briefly – Greece's third-largest city has a lively port atmosphere and a beautiful Venetian castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a bus from Patras to Athens (KTEL intercity bus, ~3 hours, ~€20). Arrive in Athens and check into a budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psyrri neighbourhood (dorm bed ~€18–25/night or private room ~€45–60). Drop bags and head out to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Monastiraki neighbourhood. Walk through the famous Monastiraki Flea Market (even in the evening, shops stay open late). Grab dinner at one of the many souvlaki joints on Mitropoleos Street – the best budget street food in Athens.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and koulouri on the Zakynthos ferry or at Killini port (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at Patras bus station or a local bakery (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki pita with tzatziki and chips on Mitropoleos Street, Athens (~€3–4 per wrap)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Athens accommodation in advance for the best budget rates. The Monastiraki and Psyrri areas are central, lively, and well-connected to all major sights. Keep your valuables secure in busy Monastiraki Square.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Acropolis (open from 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and the crowds. Climb up to see the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket for the Acropolis and surrounding sites costs €30 (or €15 off-season – confirm current price). The view over Athens from the top is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis Museum at the base of the hill (entry €10) – one of the finest museums in Europe, housing original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis. Afterwards, wander through the Plaka neighbourhood – Athens' oldest district with charming neoclassical houses, flower-draped alleys, and small churches.
day_by_day.evening: Climb Lycabettus Hill at sunset for the best panoramic view of Athens and the Acropolis lit up against the evening sky (free to walk up or take the funicular ~€7 return). Return to Monastiraki for dinner at a traditional ouzeri.

meals.breakfast: Bakery near your hostel – spanakopita and Greek coffee (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Taverna in Plaka neighbourhood – Greek salad and a mezze plate (~€9–12)
meals.dinner: Ouzeri in Monastiraki – shared mezedes (small plates): taramasalata, dolmades, grilled halloumi with ouzo (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Visit the Acropolis at opening time (8:00 AM) – it gets extremely hot and crowded by mid-morning in June. Wear comfortable shoes with grip as the marble paths can be slippery. The combined Acropolis ticket also covers the Ancient Agora, Roman Agora, Kerameikos, and other sites – use it across multiple days.

day_by_day.morning: Use your combined Acropolis ticket to visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (the heart of ancient Athenian democracy). Explore the remarkably well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the reconstructed Stoa of Attalos museum. Then visit the Roman Agora and the Tower of the Winds nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Piraeus and explore the lively fishing port. Walk along the Mikrolimano harbour – a picturesque small marina lined with seafood restaurants and sailboats. Browse the Piraeus market stalls for fresh local produce. Take a free walk along the coast to the quieter Zea Marina.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Athens. Explore the Psyrri neighbourhood – Athens' bohemian arts and nightlife district. Browse street art, small galleries, and independent shops. Find a budget psistaria (grill house) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local dairy shop near your hostel (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood mezze at a Mikrolimano harbour taverna – grilled octopus and a glass of ouzo (~€12–14)
meals.dinner: Psistaria (grill house) in Psyrri – grilled lamb chops (paidakia) with tzatziki and pita bread (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: The metro in Athens is cheap and efficient (€1.20 per trip or €4.10 for a 24-hour pass). Piraeus is just 3 stops from Monastiraki on Line 1. Mikrolimano is more expensive than typical tavernas – share dishes to keep costs down.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from Athens to Cape Sounion (~1.5 hours, ~€6.50 from Pedion Areos bus terminal). Visit the spectacular Temple of Poseidon perched on the clifftop above the Aegean Sea (entry ~€10). Lord Byron carved his name into one of the columns – look for it! The views are absolutely stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming at the small beach directly below Cape Sounion (free access). The water is crystal clear and the setting – swimming beneath an ancient Greek temple – is magical. Pack a picnic lunch to enjoy on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return bus to Athens in the late afternoon. Spend the evening exploring the Exarcheia neighbourhood – Athens' anarchist, alternative district with street art, cheap eateries, and a vibrant local atmosphere very different from the tourist areas.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita and coffee from a bakery near the bus terminal before departure (~€3)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach below Sounion – bread, local cheese, tomatoes, olives, and cold water (~€5–6)
meals.dinner: Budget taverna in Exarcheia – hearty bean soup (fasolada) or lentil soup with bread and olives (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: The bus to Sounion departs from the KTEL Attica terminal on Pedion Areos (near Pedion Areos park). Go early to avoid the midday heat at the clifftop temple. There is a small café/snack bar at the site if you need water. The last bus back to Athens departs in the early evening – check the schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Piraeus to Aegina island (~1 hour by fast ferry, ~€14 return). Aegina is one of the closest and most affordable Saronic islands from Athens. Rent a bicycle or moped on the island (bicycle ~€8/day) and cycle to the stunning Temple of Aphaia – one of the best-preserved ancient temples in Greece (entry ~€6).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle down to Aegina Town beach for a swim in the clear Saronic Gulf water. Aegina is famous for its pistachios – buy a bag of fresh local pistachios from a roadside stall (€3–4 for a generous bag). Explore the charming neoclassical port town on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the late afternoon ferry back to Piraeus. Return to Athens for your final evening in the city. Head to the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) area for an authentic, cheap dinner surrounded by locals.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri and Greek coffee from a street vendor near Piraeus port (~€2)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish taverna in Aegina Town harbour – grilled sea bream with salad (~€12–14, share a dish to save money)
meals.dinner: Taverna near the Central Market in Athens – offal soup (patsas) or bean stew with crusty bread, very local and very cheap (~€7–9)

day_by_day.notes: Buy your Aegina ferry ticket at the Piraeus port ticket booths – no advance booking needed for day trips. Aegina pistachios make excellent and affordable gifts to bring home. The island is very manageable as a day trip and gives you a taste of island life without extra accommodation costs.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus from Athens to Nafplio in the Peloponnese (~2.5 hours, ~€13.50 from Kifissos KTEL terminal). Nafplio is one of the most beautiful towns in Greece – a romantic Venetian port town with a magnificent fortress. Check bags at the bus station and explore the charming old town with its neoclassical mansions and bougainvillea-draped streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb up to the Palamidi Fortress (999 steps – or take the road) for breathtaking views over Nafplio, the Argolic Gulf, and the surrounding mountains (entry ~€8). Alternatively, take a short boat trip to the tiny Bourtzi fortress island in the middle of the harbour (~€3 return by water taxi). Swim at Arvanitia beach – a free rocky beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Syntagma Square in Nafplio's old town as the evening cools. Enjoy dinner at a traditional taverna in the backstreets. Return to Athens by evening bus, or consider staying overnight in Nafplio at a budget guesthouse (~€40–50 for a double room) for a more relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at the Athens bus terminal before departure (~€3)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros from a local grill near Nafplio's bus station (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Nafplio old town backstreets – lamb kleftiko or stuffed peppers with local Nemea wine (~€12–15)

day_by_day.notes: If budget allows, staying overnight in Nafplio is highly recommended – the town is magical in the early morning and evening without day-trip crowds. The Peloponnese has some of the best traditional Greek food in the country. Nemea wine (produced nearby) is excellent and affordable.

day_by_day.morning: If you stayed in Nafplio overnight, visit the Archaeological Museum of Nafplio on Syntagma Square (entry ~€6) – excellent collection of Mycenaean artifacts. Then take a bus or shared taxi to the ancient site of Mycenae (~45 min, ~€3–5) – the legendary Bronze Age citadel of King Agamemnon. Walk through the famous Lion Gate and explore the royal tombs (entry ~€12).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Athens by afternoon bus. Spend your last afternoon in Athens revisiting favourite spots, doing last-minute souvenir shopping at Monastiraki market, or relaxing at a rooftop café with an Acropolis view. Visit the National Garden (free) near Syntagma Square for a shaded afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens – splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at a mid-range taverna in Psyrri or Monastiraki. Try dishes you haven't had yet – perhaps lamb giouvetsi (slow-cooked with orzo pasta) or fresh grilled octopus.

meals.breakfast: Café in Nafplio – Greek coffee, fresh orange juice, and a bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Mycenae site – simple Greek salad and water (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a Psyrri taverna – lamb giouvetsi or grilled octopus with a carafe of house wine (~€15–18)

day_by_day.notes: Mycenae is one of the most important archaeological sites in the world and absolutely worth the half-day excursion. The Treasury of Atreus (Tomb of Agamemnon) near the site entrance is particularly impressive. Combined tickets may be available for Mycenae and nearby Epidaurus if you want to extend the day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Wake up early and take one last walk through the quiet morning streets of Plaka and up to the Acropolis viewpoint at Filopappou Hill (free, 15-minute walk from Monastiraki) for a final sunrise view of the Parthenon. Grab a last Greek breakfast at a local bakery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) via the metro (Line 3 direct from Monastiraki, ~40 min, €10 airport ticket). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your departure flight for check-in and security. Browse the duty-free for last-minute Greek olive oil, honey, or herbs to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Athens International Airport. Carry the memories of 13 incredible days exploring the beaches, ancient ruins, and flavours of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast – tiropita, spanakopita, and a strong Greek coffee from a Monastiraki bakery (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or pack leftovers/snacks for the journey (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: The metro to Athens airport (Line 3, blue line) departs from Monastiraki, Syntagma, and other central stations. The airport express ticket costs €10 (or €18 return). Validate your ticket before boarding. Check your airline's baggage policy if you've purchased local products to bring home – olive oil and liquids over 100ml must go in checked luggage.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer to Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island boutique stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to the boutique hotel, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Navagio Beach area to get your bearings. Enjoy the stunning clifftop views of the famous Shipwreck Beach from the viewpoint platform — no boat needed, just a short walk from the upper village.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the local rhythm with a relaxed first dinner at a nearby taverna in the village. Explore the small harbor area as the sun sets over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Light mezze plate and fresh bread at a clifftop café near the Navagio viewpoint — budget around €12–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna dinner: grilled octopus, horiatiki (village salad), and a carafe of local white wine — budget around €20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — travel fatigue is real. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance as boutique stays sometimes have limited reception hours. Exchange some euros at the airport if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning boat trip from the small port below Navagio to Shipwreck Beach (Navagio Beach) itself. Arrive early to beat the crowds — boats typically depart from around 09:00. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the iconic rusting shipwreck up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by boat and head to the nearby Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos. The afternoon light creates spectacular blue reflections inside the sea caves — take a local boat tour from Porto Vromi or Agios Nikolaos port (approx. €15–20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Head into the village of Anafonitria or nearby Volimes for dinner. Browse the local honey and nougat shops before the evening meal.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the boutique hotel or a nearby café — yogurt with thyme honey, fresh fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed snack or light bite on the boat — bring water and a sandwich from a local bakery. Alternatively, grab a gyros wrap at a small kiosk near the port for €4–6.
meals.dinner: Family-run taverna in Volimes village — try lamb kleftiko (slow-baked lamb) and tzatziki with warm pita. Budget €18–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Navagio boat trip the evening before or first thing in the morning — it sells out quickly in June. Wear reef-safe sunscreen and bring water shoes as the beach is pebbly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Venetian-era village of Anafonitria and the Monastery of Agios Dionysios of Anafonitria, a peaceful 15th-century monastery set among olive groves. The drive through the northern highlands offers breathtaking views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Porto Limnionas, a secluded rocky cove on the west coast accessible by a short hike. Swim in the vivid emerald-green water sheltered by limestone cliffs — one of Zakynthos's hidden gems.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Navagio area for a clifftop sunset cocktail at a bar overlooking the bay. The golden-hour light on the white cliffs is extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Anafonitria village — Greek coffee, tiropita (cheese pastry), and fresh orange juice. Budget €6–8.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch sourced from a local mini-market: olives, local cheese (graviera), tomatoes, crusty bread, and cold water — budget €8–10.
meals.dinner: Grilled fish dinner at a small taverna near the hotel — fresh catch of the day, Greek salad, and local retsina or Robola wine. Budget €22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The road to Porto Limnionas is narrow and partially unpaved — a small rental car or scooter is ideal. Wear good sandals for the rocky cove.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a car or join a guided tour to explore Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) on the eastern coast. Visit the Byzantine Museum in Solomos Square, which houses an impressive collection of post-Byzantine icons rescued from island churches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along the Zakynthos Town waterfront promenade. Visit the Venetian Castle (Kastro) perched above the town for panoramic views across the island and the Ionian Sea. Walk through the arcaded streets of the Venetian-influenced town center.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Zakynthos Town's lively harbor area, which has a great selection of mid-range restaurants and live Greek music in some venues.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery stop on the drive — spanakopita (spinach pie) and a Freddo cappuccino, a Greek staple.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a harbor-front restaurant in Zakynthos Town — moussaka, dakos salad, and a cold Mythos beer. Budget €15–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in the old town with live traditional Greek music — souvlaki platter, grilled vegetables, and local wine. Budget €20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Town is about a 45-minute drive from Navagio. Parking near the waterfront can be busy — arrive early or use a paid lot. The Byzantine Museum is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south to Laganas Bay and visit the Caretta Caretta (loggerhead sea turtle) information center. Zakynthos is one of the most important nesting sites in the Mediterranean — learn about conservation efforts and morning turtle spotting protocols.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Gerakas Beach, a protected sea turtle nesting beach on the southeastern tip of the island. Swimming is permitted in designated areas and the beach is stunning — fine golden sand and clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the village of Keri on the return journey for sunset views from the Keri Lighthouse and Keri Cliffs. The dramatic sea stacks and arches are beautiful at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before the long drive south.
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a taverna near Gerakas — grilled sea bream, calamari, and a Greek salad. Budget €18–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Simple, hearty dinner back near the hotel — stuffed tomatoes (gemista), lentil soup, and local bread at a village taverna. Budget €14–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has strict rules to protect turtle nests — no umbrellas in certain zones, no access after sunset. Respect all signage. The drive south is scenic but takes about 1.5 hours from Navagio.

day_by_day.morning: A slower morning — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take a morning swim at a quieter local beach near Navagio. Explore the village of Exo Hora on foot, a charming traditional settlement with old stone houses and a central square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a kayaking or stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session along the northern coastline. Several operators near Porto Vromi offer half-day guided sea kayak tours through sea caves and hidden coves — budget €35–45 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Enjoy a drink on the terrace watching the sunset, then head out for a casual dinner close by.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a clifftop café — Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a double espresso.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beach snack bar — club sandwich or a Greek wrap with tzatziki and grilled chicken. Budget €10–13.
meals.dinner: Mezze-style dinner at a local taverna — a spread of small plates: taramosalata, gigantes beans, saganaki (fried cheese), grilled pita. Budget €16–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Day 6 is intentionally relaxed — a mid-trip rest day prevents burnout. Book the kayaking session the day before to secure a spot.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Zakynthos to Kefalonia (Sami or Poros port — approximately 1.5–2 hour crossing). Arrive and check in briefly, then head to Melissani Cave — a stunning underground lake where sunlight filters through a collapsed roof, turning the water an ethereal blue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Drogarati Cave nearby, a vast stalactite cavern with remarkable acoustics. Then drive to Antisamos Beach, a dramatic pebble beach with vivid turquoise water backed by green hills — made famous by the film 'Captain Corelli's Mandolin.'
day_by_day.evening: Explore the port town of Sami or drive to the village of Agia Efimia for dinner overlooking the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the ferry — grab pastries and coffee to go if needed.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna near Antisamos Beach — fresh calamari, Greek salad, and cold water. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Harborside dinner in Agia Efimia — grilled lobster pasta or fresh fish with local Kefalonian Robola white wine. Budget €22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the ferry in advance — June is busy and foot-passenger tickets sell out. The Melissani Cave boat tour costs approximately €8–10. Antisamos is pebbly — water shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Drive across Kefalonia to the capital, Argostoli. Visit the Korgialenios History and Folklore Museum to understand the island's history, including the devastating 1953 earthquake. Walk through the lively central market and Lithostroto pedestrian street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Myrtos Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches — a dramatic arc of white pebbles and electric-blue water framed by towering white limestone cliffs. Swim and relax through the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Argostoli for the evening. Join the locals for the traditional evening volta (stroll) along the waterfront. Watch the famous Kefalonian loggerhead turtles that gather at the harbor at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Argostoli — bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and Greek coffee at a local café on the main square.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Myrtos Beach — buy supplies from a Argostoli deli: local cheese, cured meats, olives, and bread.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Argostoli at a mid-range restaurant — meat pie (kreatopita), village sausages, and a carafe of local wine. Budget €20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has limited shade — bring your own umbrella or rent one. The road down to the beach is steep and winding. Parking is at the top; walk down about 10 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Fiskardo village on the northern tip of Kefalonia — the only village that survived the 1953 earthquake intact. It retains its original Venetian architecture and is incredibly picturesque. Wander the harbor and browse the small artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short boat trip from Fiskardo to the nearby island of Ithaca (Ithaki) — the legendary home of Odysseus. Explore the small capital Vathy with its neoclassical mansions and Archaeological Museum. Swim at a quiet beach cove.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fiskardo by boat for dinner in one of its charming harbor restaurants before driving back to your Kefalonia base.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Fiskardo — fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee while watching the yachts in the harbor.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Vathy, Ithaca — simple taverna meal: grilled chicken souvlaki, tzatziki, and salad. Budget €14–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fiskardo harbor — fresh lobster or grilled whole fish with local wine at a slightly splurge-worthy harborside restaurant. Budget €28–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Fiskardo is the most upscale village in Kefalonia — prices are slightly higher. The Ithaca day trip is best arranged with a local boat operator in Fiskardo the evening before. Budget €20–25 per person for the crossing.

day_by_day.morning: Return by ferry to Zakynthos in the morning. Relax on the crossing and enjoy the sea views. Check back in to the Navagio boutique hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend a slow afternoon at a beach near the hotel — perhaps revisit Navagio from the clifftop viewpoint or find a quiet rocky cove for a final swim. Read, nap, and recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Revisit a favorite local taverna from earlier in the trip for a nostalgic dinner. Treat yourself to a local dessert — loukoumades (honey-drenched doughnuts) or galaktoboureko (custard pastry).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Kefalonia hotel before the ferry.
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the ferry or at a café near the Zakynthos port upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Return to your favorite Navagio-area taverna — order anything you loved earlier in the trip. Budget €18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the return ferry in advance. Day 10 is a transition and recovery day — keep it low-key intentionally before the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day boat excursion from Porto Vromi — many operators offer combined trips to Navagio Beach, the Blue Caves, and snorkeling stops at hidden coves along the northern coast. This is the most comprehensive way to see Zakynthos's coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the boat tour — snorkeling at a secluded cove with rich marine life. The Ionian Sea here is exceptionally clear and warm in June. Relax on the deck between stops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to port by late afternoon. Shower and head out for a final clifftop sunset experience. Pick up some local souvenirs — Zakynthos honey, local olive oil, and nougat (mandolato) from village shops.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the hotel before the early boat departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch provided on the boat tour (most full-day tours include a BBQ or light meal on board) — confirm when booking.
meals.dinner: Celebratory penultimate dinner — try a restaurant with a full mezze spread and live Greek music if available. Budget €22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Full-day boat tours from Porto Vromi cost approximately €40–55 per person and typically run 09:00–17:00. Bring sunscreen, a hat, a towel, and snorkeling gear (or rent on board).

day_by_day.morning: Spend a final relaxed morning at the most beautiful beach you discovered during the trip. Take one last swim in the warm Ionian Sea. Reflect on the journey over a long Greek coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pack, check out of the boutique hotel, and do a final drive around the northern Zakynthos highlands. Stop at local artisan shops in Volimes to buy last-minute gifts — handmade lace, local spirits (tsipourou), and honey products.
day_by_day.evening: Early evening arrival at Zakynthos Town for a final dinner in the harbor area. Stroll the waterfront one last time and enjoy the warm June evening.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — make it count. Enjoy everything on offer.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a clifftop café near Navagio — one last view of the famous bay.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Zakynthos Town harbor — fresh grilled fish, a full Greek salad, and a bottle of chilled Assyrtiko white wine. Budget €25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time carefully. If your flight is the next day, consider staying overnight near the airport or in Zakynthos Town to avoid an early-morning rush from the north of the island.

day_by_day.morning: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final Greek breakfast — freddo espresso, a warm koulouri (sesame bread ring), and fresh fruit at a café near the airport or in Zakynthos Town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Zakynthos Airport for departure. Arrive at least 2 hours before your flight. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Greek products — olive oil, herbs, and local sweets make great gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home the memories of turquoise waters, sun-warmed cliffs, grilled fish, and the warmth of Greek hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at an airport café or a nearby town café — yogurt, honey, pastry, and strong Greek coffee.
meals.lunch: Airport meal or a packed snack from a local bakery if departing midday.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your destination.

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Airport (ZTH) is small — security lines can move slowly in peak season. Arrive with plenty of time. Double-check all luggage for fragile souvenir items like olive oil bottles. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from the airport to your boutique stay at Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island. Enjoy the scenic coastal drive and settle into your luxury suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique property and refresh. Take a private guided orientation walk along the clifftops above Navagio Beach for breathtaking panoramic views of the iconic Shipwreck Beach from above. Enjoy a welcome glass of chilled Assyrtiko wine on your terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's clifftop bar overlooking the Ionian Sea. Enjoy a leisurely welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring fresh Zakynthian seafood and local specialties.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light mezze platter and fresh juice at the hotel upon check-in
meals.dinner: Hotel signature restaurant — grilled octopus, fresh sea bass with capers and local herbs, paired with Robola white wine from Kefalonia

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm boutique stay welcome package. Keep the afternoon light given travel fatigue. Sea temperature around 24°C — perfect for a quick dip if energy allows.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach — access the iconic cove by sea, arriving before the day-trippers for an exclusive early-morning swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters. Snorkeling equipment provided. Explore the famous rusted shipwreck MV Panagiotis up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the private boat tour along the northern Zakynthos coastline, exploring the Blue Caves at Cape Skinari. The midday sun creates spectacular azure light reflections inside the sea caves. Swim in the cave waters and enjoy a chilled champagne and fresh fruit spread on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay by late afternoon. Freshen up and head to a nearby clifftop taverna in the village of Anafonitria for a traditional Zakynthian dinner with panoramic sunset views over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel — local honey, fresh figs, Zakynthian cheese (ladotyri), yogurt, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the private boat — smoked salmon, local olives, artisan cheeses, crusty bread, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Taverna Anafonitria — slow-braised lamb with rosemary, grilled red mullet, horta (wild greens), and local Verdea wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat in advance — early morning departure recommended (08:00) to beat crowds at Navagio. Apply high SPF sunscreen; temperatures will reach 29°C on the water. Bring a hat and light cover-up.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) — explore the Venetian-influenced architecture, the elegant Solomos Square, the Byzantine Museum with its remarkable collection of post-Byzantine icons, and the hilltop Venetian Castle with sweeping views over the town and bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the local Zakynthos market and artisan shops in the old town. Sample local specialties including mandolato (nougat), pasteli (sesame honey bars), and Zakynthian olive oil. Stop at a premium deli to select artisan products. Afternoon leisure at a luxury beach club on the calmer east coast of the island.
day_by_day.evening: Private dinner reservation at one of Zakynthos Town's finest waterfront restaurants. Enjoy refined Greek cuisine with a modern twist alongside views of the illuminated harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel terrace breakfast — freshly squeezed orange juice, Greek pastries, soft-boiled eggs, and local cold cuts
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — grilled calamari, Greek salad with Kefalograviera cheese, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Waterfront fine dining — lobster pasta with bisque sauce, grilled swordfish with lemon caper butter, and a bottle of Gaia Thalassitis Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Town is approximately 40 minutes by car from Navagio Beach — arrange private driver. Byzantine Museum is closed on Mondays; confirm opening hours. Market is most vibrant in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the boutique stay — private yoga session on the clifftop terrace at sunrise, followed by a long breakfast. Spend time reading and relaxing by the infinity pool with views over the Ionian Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour to the Venetian village of Keri and the Keri Lighthouse at the southern tip of Zakynthos. Explore the dramatic sea caves and natural tar springs (historically used by ancient sailors). Swim at the secluded Limni Keriou beach, known for its calm, clear waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a premium taverna in Keri village — one of the most spectacular sunset vantage points on the island. Enjoy traditional Zakynthian cuisine in a relaxed village atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — smoked trout, avocado on sourdough, fresh fruit platter, and specialty Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — watermelon and feta salad, grilled halloumi skewers, and chilled cucumber gazpacho
meals.dinner: Keri village taverna — fresh grilled sea bream, stuffed courgette flowers, tzatziki, and local house wine

day_by_day.notes: Keri Lighthouse offers one of the best sunset views on the island — arrive by 19:30 for the best light. The tar springs at Keri are a unique geological curiosity mentioned by Herodotus. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for the lighthouse path.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat transfer from Zakynthos to Kefalonia Island (approximately 1.5 hours). Arrive at Fiskardo, the island's most picturesque Venetian harbor village. Check in to a luxury boutique property in Fiskardo and explore the charming harbor on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Myrtos Beach — one of the most photographed beaches in Greece, with dramatic white pebbles and vivid turquoise water framed by towering limestone cliffs. Arrive by private car and enjoy a premium beach experience with sunbeds and service.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fiskardo for a leisurely harbor-side dinner. The village comes alive in the evening with yachts moored in the harbor and a sophisticated dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Navagio boutique stay before departure — full spread with local specialties
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the boat crew enjoyed en route or on arrival in Fiskardo — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, and chilled water
meals.dinner: Tassia Restaurant, Fiskardo — an iconic Kefalonian institution serving exceptional fresh seafood and local specialties; try the Kefalonian meat pie and fresh lobster

day_by_day.notes: Confirm speedboat charter and weather conditions the day before. Fiskardo was the only village on Kefalonia to survive the devastating 1953 earthquake, preserving its Venetian architecture. Myrtos Beach has limited shade — bring parasol and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Melissani Cave and Lake — an extraordinary underground lake where sunlight pierces a collapsed cave ceiling to create magical turquoise reflections. Arrive early to experience it before tour groups arrive. Nearby, visit the Drogarati Cave with its impressive stalactites and stalagmites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic capital of Kefalonia, Argostoli. Visit the Korgialenios History and Folklore Museum, stroll the elegant De Bosset Bridge (the longest stone bridge over seawater in the world), and browse the vibrant central market. Stop at a premium deli for Kefalonian specialties including Robola wine and local honey.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing trip around the Argostoli Bay, with a stop to observe the famous Kefalonian loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) in their natural habitat. Return to Fiskardo for a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Fiskardo — Greek yogurt with Kefalonian honey and walnuts, fresh pastries, and Nescafé frappé
meals.lunch: Argostoli waterfront café — grilled octopus salad, dakos (Cretan-style rusk with tomato), and fresh fish soup
meals.dinner: Fiskardo harbor restaurant — pan-seared red snapper, seafood risotto with local herbs, and a bottle of Robola of Kefalonia white wine

day_by_day.notes: Melissani Cave boat tours run on a schedule — book the first entry slot (around 08:30) for the best light effect when the sun is directly overhead (best between 11:00–13:00 in summer). Sea turtle observation must be done respectfully — maintain distance and no flash photography.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning in Fiskardo — swim from the small pebble beach near the harbor, explore the Venetian lighthouse ruins, and browse the boutique shops along the waterfront. Optional: private kayaking around the Fiskardo peninsula to discover hidden coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion to the secluded Antisamos Beach (famously used as a filming location for Captain Corelli's Mandolin) and the nearby Agia Efimia village. Swim in the gin-clear waters and enjoy a relaxed afternoon on the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Fiskardo at a premium waterfront restaurant. Enjoy a long, leisurely meal watching the superyachts in the harbor as the sun sets.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Fiskardo village — fresh orange juice, croissants, local jam, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: On-boat lunch at Antisamos — cold cuts, fresh bread, hummus, tabbouleh, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Vasso's Restaurant, Fiskardo — fresh crayfish, grilled catch of the day, and homemade baklava with Kefalonian honey ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Antisamos Beach is pebbly but the water clarity is exceptional — water shoes recommended. Agia Efimia is a quieter alternative to Fiskardo with excellent local tavernas. Confirm onward ferry or speedboat to Lefkada for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer and ferry from Kefalonia to Lefkada Island. Arrive at Lefkada Town and check in to a luxury boutique hotel. Explore the unique wooden-framed Venetian architecture of Lefkada Town, which was designed to withstand earthquakes. Visit the 14th-century Santa Maura Fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to Porto Katsiki Beach — consistently ranked among the top beaches in Europe, with dramatic white limestone cliffs plunging into electric-blue water. Arrive by private boat from the south for the most exclusive access and spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lefkada Town for an evening stroll along the marina and a premium dinner at one of the island's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Fiskardo before departure — full Greek spread
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a taverna near Porto Katsiki or on the private boat — grilled prawns, fresh bread, and Greek salad
meals.dinner: Lefkada Town fine dining — lamb chops with mint yogurt, stuffed peppers with rice and herbs, and local Lefkadian wine

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki has limited beach access by land (steep stairs) — arriving by boat is more comfortable and exclusive. Lefkada is connected to the mainland by a floating bridge, making it technically a peninsula. The town's distinctive architecture is worth exploring on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour to Egremni Beach — a remote, stunning beach accessible by a long staircase or by boat. Arrive by private boat for an exclusive morning swim in one of the most unspoiled beaches in the Ionian Islands. Snorkeling in the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming village of Sivota on the east coast of Lefkada — a picturesque fishing village with turquoise lagoon waters. Explore the village on foot, visit the small church, and take a kayak or paddleboard out on the calm lagoon waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Agios Nikitas village, followed by dinner at a premium taverna in this charming whitewashed village on Lefkada's west coast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit, Greek pastries, eggs to order, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Sivota waterfront taverna — fresh mussels, grilled fish, and chilled local white wine
meals.dinner: Agios Nikitas taverna — slow-roasted goat with herbs, grilled aubergine with feta, and homemade tiramisu with Greek twist

day_by_day.notes: Egremni Beach was damaged by a 2015 earthquake and the staircase was rebuilt — confirm current access conditions. Sivota lagoon is best explored in the early afternoon when the light is best for photography. Agios Nikitas is one of the most charming villages on Lefkada.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the hotel — spa treatment (deep tissue massage or traditional Greek herbal treatment), followed by a late breakfast by the pool. Optional: private yoga or Pilates session on the hotel terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided food tour of Lefkada — visit local producers of the island's famous salted cod (bakaliaros), the local meat products, and the Lefkadian olive oil cooperatives. Taste and purchase premium local products to take home. Visit a local winery for a private tasting of indigenous Lefkadian varieties.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset boat cruise around the southern tip of Lefkada, passing Skorpios Island (the private island once owned by Aristotle Onassis). Champagne and canapés served on board as the sun sets over the Ionian Sea.

meals.breakfast: Extended spa breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, poached eggs, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Food tour tasting lunch — an array of local specialties including salted cod fritters, local cheeses, cured meats, and fresh bread
meals.dinner: Premium waterfront restaurant in Lefkada Town — seafood linguine with bottarga, grilled whole lobster, and a bottle of Domaine Sigalas Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: The Lefkada food tour should be booked with a specialist local guide. Skorpios Island is privately owned (purchased by the Onassis family and later by Russian oligarch Rybolovlev) — boat access is restricted to the waters around it. Sunset cruise timing depends on sunset (approximately 20:45 in June).

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer and ferry from Lefkada to Corfu (Kerkyra). Check in to a luxury property in Corfu Town or the north of the island. Begin exploring Corfu Town — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Walk through the Venetian-era Campiello district, the narrow alleyways (kantounia), and visit the imposing Old Fortress.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the elegant Achilleion Palace — the neoclassical summer residence built for Empress Elisabeth of Austria (Sisi), surrounded by terraced gardens with statues of Achilles and sweeping views over the Ionian Sea. Explore the palace museum and stroll the manicured gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Evening promenade along the Liston — Corfu Town's elegant arcaded promenade modeled on the Rue de Rivoli in Paris. Aperitivo at one of the historic cafés, followed by a premium dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast on the ferry or at the hotel upon arrival
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Corfiot restaurant in the old town — pastitsada (rooster braised in spiced tomato sauce), sofrito (veal in white wine and garlic), and local beer
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Corfu Town — Corfiot bourdeto (spicy fish stew), grilled langoustines, and a bottle of Theotoky Estate white wine

day_by_day.notes: Corfu Town's UNESCO World Heritage status means the old town is beautifully preserved — allow time to get pleasantly lost in the alleyways. The Achilleion Palace is 12km from Corfu Town — private driver recommended. Book dinner in advance as top restaurants fill quickly in June.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion to the Diapontia Islands (Othoni, Erikoussa, and Mathraki) — a remote archipelago northwest of Corfu rarely visited by tourists. Swim in pristine, uncrowded waters, explore the tiny fishing villages, and enjoy the unspoiled natural beauty of these hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Corfu and visit the beautiful village of Paleokastritsa on the west coast — a stunning bay with multiple coves of turquoise water, dramatic cliffs, and a 13th-century Byzantine monastery perched on a headland. Swim in the clearest water of the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium dinner on Corfu — a special tasting menu at one of the island's most acclaimed restaurants, celebrating the culinary journey through the Ionian Islands.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure — full Greek spread with fresh juice and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a small taverna on Erikoussa Island — grilled fish caught that morning, village salad, and local wine
meals.dinner: Tasting menu dinner — seven-course Corfiot and Ionian-inspired menu with wine pairing, featuring local ingredients and modern Greek culinary techniques

day_by_day.notes: The Diapontia Islands excursion requires an early start (07:00) due to the distance — confirm weather and sea conditions the day before. Paleokastritsa Monastery has a dress code (shoulders and knees covered). The evening tasting menu restaurant should be booked well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning in Corfu — last swim at a favorite beach, final Greek coffee at a harbor café, and last-minute shopping for premium local products: Corfiot kumquat liqueur, local olive oil, and artisan ceramics. Visit the Municipal Gallery of Corfu for a curated collection of Corfiot art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Corfu International Airport (Ioannis Kapodistrias Airport) for departure. Depending on flight time, enjoy a final lunch at an airport-area restaurant or at the hotel before checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Corfu. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the best beaches, flavors, and hidden gems of the Ionian Islands — Zakynthos, Kefalonia, Lefkada, and Corfu.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at the hotel — a full celebratory spread with all favorite items from the trip: yogurt with honey, fresh pastries, local cheeses, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a waterfront restaurant near the airport — grilled fish, Greek salad, and a final glass of chilled Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security at Corfu Airport, which can be busy in peak summer season. Arrange private airport transfer. Ensure all purchased local products (liquids, olive oil) comply with airline carry-on regulations — checked luggage recommended for liquids. Consider purchasing a premium hamper of Ionian Island specialties as a final souvenir.
